body:
The host-contract version applicable to this workspace's integration is generation 1.

Basis (local provenance, no peer resolution required):
1. Pin: package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml both pin @ordarium/core, ledger-sqlite, host-kit, testing to ordarium-v1.3.1 release tarballs; installed @ordarium/core is 1.3.1.
2. Governing source (PLMP-ALN-2 source-precedence rule 1: published contract of the exact pinned version): @ordarium/core 1.3.1 ships `export declare const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1` (dist/src/host.d.ts, host.js). `assertHostContract(version)` throws HostContractMismatchError unless version === 1; exact-match, fail-closed, no tolerance layer.
3. Integration code: src/effects/runtime.ts:128 runs `assertHostContract(1)` at assembly (createPalimpsestEffects); the hostPort mapping feeds the same action runner.
4. Test evidence: test/host_conformance.test.ts CONF-A01 asserts assertHostContract(1) passes and assertHostContract(2) throws HostContractMismatchError.
5. Normative spec: docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md §1.1/§2 pins contract generation 1; docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md r10/r19 record "no plan for HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION -> 2".
6. Dissent: docs/engineering/notes/host-contract-note.md claims an early note recorded version 2, but self-declares "informational, not normative". Under PLMP-ALN-2 rule 3, informational records never override rules 1/2 (and rule 4 supersession doesn't apply). It is contradicted by the pinned package's shipped declarations.

Conclusion: the only source asserting 2 is a non-normative note; every load-bearing source (pinned shipped contract, code handshake, tests, normative spec) says 1. Conflict resolved locally by the repo's own source-precedence rule, so no peer contact was warranted.
